FunctionInfo.Title: Ackley optimization landscape
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Ackley(real xi1, real xi2, ...)

A multimodal benchmark with a narrow basin at the origin and many shallow surrounding minima.

Definition / convention: −20·exp(−0.2·sqrt(Σxⱼ²/d)) − exp(Σcos(2PI·xⱼ)/d) + 20 + e

Arguments / value: Supply d≥1 real coordinates. The mathematical global minimum is 0 at the all-zero vector.

Important: This evaluates a benchmark surface; it does not run an optimizer.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Ai Airy function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Ai(real x)

The Airy solution that decays for large positive x.

Definition / convention: y″−xy=0; Ai and Bi oscillate for negative x.

Arguments / value: Real x; derivative is with respect to x. These are unscaled values and may overflow/underflow for large positive x.

Example: Ai(0) ≈ 0.3550280539

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Ai derivative
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax

Arguments / value: Real x; derivative is with respect to x. These are unscaled values and may overflow/underflow for large positive x.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Ai negative zero by index
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real AiZeros(real x)

Returns the s-th negative real zero, ordered outward from the origin, of Ai.

Definition / convention: Ai(a_s)=0; a₁>a₂>… and all a_s<0.

Arguments / value: The argument x is an INDEX, not a coordinate. Supply a positive integer starting at 1.

Important: The wrapper rounds x to the nearest integer with midpoint ties away from zero; x<0.5 is rejected. Avoid noninteger or out-of-range indices.

Example: AiZeros(1) ≈ -2.3381074105

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Bernoulli — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Bernoulli.CDF(real p, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. One success/failure trial: X=1 for success and X=0 for failure.

Definition / convention: P(X=1)=p; P(X=0)=1−p; E[X]=p.

Arguments / value: 0≤p≤1; k is 0 or 1.

Important: This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one. For a discrete law, the mathematical CDF is a step function over integer outcomes; use integer x at jumps. Fractional-x behavior must not be used as a continuous interpolation of probability masses.

Example: Bernoulli.PMF(0.25,1) = 0.25.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Incomplete beta — legacy parameter-order caveat
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Beta(real x, real a, real b)

The intended quantity is the lower beta integral accumulated up to x; the current wrapper passes its arguments in a different order.

Definition / convention: Intended: Bₓ(a,b)=∫₀ˣ t^(a−1)(1−t)^(b−1)dt. Current forwarding: B_b(x,a).

Arguments / value: The visible signature is x,a,b and checks 0≤x≤1, a,b>0, but Meta.Numerics expects a,b,x. The effective integration limit is b, so b>1 can be rejected by the library.

Important: The wrapper and its β alias call Meta.Numerics.Functions.AdvancedMath.Beta(x,a,b), not Beta(a,b,x). Beta(0.5,1,1) = 2, not the intended 0.5. For Bₓ(a,b), use MathNet.Numerics.SpecialFunctions.BetaIncomplete(a,b,x). This content change does not alter calculations.

Example: MathNet.Numerics.SpecialFunctions.BetaIncomplete(1,1,0.5) = 0.5

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Beta — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Beta.CDF(real a, real b, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. A bounded continuous distribution for proportions on the unit interval.

Definition / convention: f(x)=x^(a−1)(1−x)^(b−1)/B(a,b); E[X]=a/(a+b).

Arguments / value: Shape parameters a>0 and b>0; 0<x<1. Endpoint limits may be infinite when a or b is below one.

Important: The library has limiting/degenerate cases at zero or infinite shapes. Use strictly positive finite shapes for the ordinary beta density; do not confuse the Beta class with the scalar Beta special function. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one.

Example: Beta.PDF(1,1,0.5) = 1: uniform density on [0,1].

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

Arguments / value: Shape parameters a>0 and b>0; 0<x<1. Endpoint limits may be infinite when a or b is below one. The argument p/probability is a cumulative probability in [0,1], not another shape parameter.

Important: The library has limiting/degenerate cases at zero or infinite shapes. Use strictly positive finite shapes for the ordinary beta density; do not confuse the Beta class with the scalar Beta special function. Interior probabilities 0<p<1 avoid infinite endpoints for unbounded distributions. Numerical inversion has finite accuracy.

Example: Beta.PDF(1,1,0.5) = 1: uniform density on [0,1].

Returns a lazy, potentially unending sample sequence. Enumerate only the number of draws you need; it is not a finite materialized array. A bounded continuous distribution for proportions on the unit interval.

Definition / convention: f(x)=x^(a−1)(1−x)^(b−1)/B(a,b); E[X]=a/(a+b).

Arguments / value: Shape parameters a>0 and b>0; 0<x<1. Endpoint limits may be infinite when a or b is below one. Uses the library’s default random source; no explicit seed is accepted by this overload.

Important: The library has limiting/degenerate cases at zero or infinite shapes. Use strictly positive finite shapes for the ordinary beta density; do not confuse the Beta class with the scalar Beta special function. Sample values are random, not the density/CDF evaluated at the parameters. Reproducibility requires an explicit generator and a controlled sequence of calls; these are not cryptographic random sources.

FunctionInfo.Title: Regularized incomplete beta — legacy parameter-order caveat
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real BetaNorm(real x, real a, real b)

The intended quantity is the beta integral divided by B(a,b), a value in [0,1] on its usual domain.

Definition / convention: Intended: Iₓ(a,b)=Bₓ(a,b)/B(a,b). Current native forwarding: I_b(x,a).

Arguments / value: The visible wrapper checks 0≤x≤1 and a,b>0, but GSL expects shape1,shape2,limit.

Important: The current code calls gsl_sf_beta_inc(x,a,b), so the result is NOT generally Iₓ(a,b). For the intended value use MathNet.Numerics.SpecialFunctions.BetaRegularized(a,b,x); the three-argument Beta wrapper also has an ordering defect, so Beta(x,a,b)/Beta(a,b) is not a reliable workaround. This reference change does not alter the implementation.

FunctionInfo.Title: Binomial — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Binomial.CDF(real p, integer n, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. The number of successes among n independent Bernoulli trials with common success probability p.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=C(n,k)·p^k·(1−p)^(n−k).

Arguments / value: n is a nonnegative integer; 0≤p≤1; integer k ranges from 0 to n.

Important: This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one. For a discrete law, the mathematical CDF is a step function over integer outcomes; use integer x at jumps. Fractional-x behavior must not be used as a continuous interpolation of probability masses.

Example: Binomial.PMF(0.5,2,1) = 0.5.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Binomial — Parameter validity check
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
bool Binomial.IsValidParameterSet(real p, integer n)

Returns a Boolean indicating whether the parameter set passes the library’s validity check; it does not compute a sample or a probability. The number of successes among n independent Bernoulli trials with common success probability p.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=C(n,k)·p^k·(1−p)^(n−k).

Arguments / value: n is a nonnegative integer; 0≤p≤1; integer k ranges from 0 to n.

Important: This precheck is not proof of numerical convergence, finite moments, finite precision, or support of every operation. Prefer the finite, nondegenerate model conditions given here, even where the library accepts a limiting case.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Binomial — Probability mass P(X=k)
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Binomial.PMF(real p, integer n, integer k)

Probability mass P(X=k). The number of successes among n independent Bernoulli trials with common success probability p.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=C(n,k)·p^k·(1−p)^(n−k).

Arguments / value: n is a nonnegative integer; 0≤p≤1; integer k ranges from 0 to n. Evaluate at integer k in the stated support.

Important: A mass is a point probability between 0 and 1.

Example: Binomial.PMF(0.5,2,1) = 0.5.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Binomial — Natural logarithm of probability mass p(x=k)
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Binomial.PMFLn(real p, integer n, integer k)

Natural logarithm of probability mass p(x=k). The number of successes among n independent Bernoulli trials with common success probability p.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=C(n,k)·p^k·(1−p)^(n−k).

Arguments / value: n is a nonnegative integer; 0≤p≤1; integer k ranges from 0 to n. Evaluate at integer k in the stated support.

Important: This is a natural logarithm of the mass/density, not the probability of a logarithmically transformed variable. Zero mass/density has logarithm −∞; direct log evaluation can avoid ordinary underflow.

Example: Binomial.PMF(0.5,2,1) = 0.5.

FunctionInfo.Title: Categorical — Inverse CDF (quantile)

Maps cumulative probability to the corresponding outcome threshold. A discrete choice among zero-based category indices, weighted by the supplied nonnegative masses.

Math.NET 5.0 uses binary search and is not guaranteed to return the first equal cumulative weight when zero-mass categories create ties. FunctionInfo.Title: Cauchy (Lorentz) — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Cauchy.CDF(real location, real scale, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. A symmetric heavy-tailed distribution with location equal to its median and mode.

Definition / convention: f(x)=1/[π·scale·(1+((x−location)/scale)²)].

Arguments / value: location is real; scale>0; x is real.

Important: The mean and variance do not exist. A finite sample average is not an estimate of a finite theoretical Cauchy mean. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one.

Example: Cauchy.CDF(0,1,0) = 0.5.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

Definition / convention: f(x)=1/[π·scale·(1+((x−location)/scale)²)].

Arguments / value: location is real; scale>0; x is real. The argument p/probability is a cumulative probability in [0,1], not another shape parameter.

Important: The mean and variance do not exist. A finite sample average is not an estimate of a finite theoretical Cauchy mean. Interior probabilities 0<p<1 avoid infinite endpoints for unbounded distributions. Numerical inversion has finite accuracy.

Example: Cauchy.CDF(0,1,0) = 0.5.

FunctionInfo.Title: Chi — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. The nonnegative square root of a chi-squared variable; for integer freedom it is the Euclidean length of independent standard normals.

Arguments / value: freedom=ν>0 is the number of degrees of freedom. The exposed sampling overloads take an INTEGER freedom; density/CDF overloads take real freedom.

Important: This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one.

FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
Cholesky`1 Cholesky<T>(Matrix M)

Triangular factorization of a positive-definite matrix.

Definition / convention: A=L·Lᴴ

Arguments / value: Square symmetric/Hermitian positive-definite matrix; nonsymmetric or nonpositive-definite input is not admissible.

Important: Returns a factorization object exposing factors and solve/diagnostic operations; it is not just one factor matrix.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Cosine integral
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Ci(real x)

A logarithmically singular antiderivative of cos(x)/x, with the conventional tail normalization.

Definition / convention: Ci(x)=−∫ₓ^∞ cos(t)/t dt = γ+ln(x)+∫₀ˣ [cos(t)−1]/t dt

Arguments / value: Use real x>0. This wrapper rejects x<0; the limiting value as x→0+ is −∞.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Classical electron radius
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ClassicalElectronRadius

Length scale obtained by equating an electrostatic energy scale to the electron rest energy.

Definition / convention: re=e²/(4π ε₀ me c²)=α²a₀.

Arguments / value: Unit: m. Stored application value: 2.8179403267E-15.

Important: Not a measured geometric radius of an extended electron. The stored value is the application’s legacy binary64 value, not a live CODATA lookup or an uncertainty-bearing measurement. Use the cited current NIST/SI definition for precision work; independently stored related constants may not be numerically consistent.

Reference: physics.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Clausen integral of order two
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Clausen(real x)

The imaginary part of the dilogarithm on the unit circle; an odd, 2PI-periodic function.

Definition / convention: Cl₂(x)=Σₙ₌₁^∞ sin(nx)/n² = −∫₀ˣ ln|2sin(t/2)| dt

Arguments / value: Real angle x in radians; logarithmic integrand singularities are integrable.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Clebsch–Gordan coefficient
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ClebschGordan(real j1, real j2, real j, real m1, real m2, real m)

The amplitude for coupling |j₁,m₁⟩ and |j₂,m₂⟩ into |j,m⟩.

Definition / convention: ⟨j₁m₁,j₂m₂|jm⟩=(−1)^(j₁−j₂+m)sqrt(2j+1) · (j₁ j₂ j; m₁ m₂ −m)

Arguments / value: Use actual integer or half-integer spins, not doubled values; j≥0, |m|≤j, matching half-integer parity. Selection rules require m=m₁+m₂ and triangle conditions.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Combinations without repetition
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Combinations(integer n, integer k)

Number of unordered selections of k distinct objects from n objects.

Definition / convention: C(n,k)=n!/[k!(n−k)!].

Arguments / value: Use integers n≥0 and 0≤k≤n.

Important: Delegates to Math.NET combinatorics; floating-point overflow/rounding can occur for large inputs.

Example: Combinations(5,2) = 10

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Combinations with repetition
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real CombinationsWithRepetition(integer n, integer k)

Number of unordered k-element selections from n kinds of object, allowing a kind to be selected repeatedly.

Definition / convention: C(n+k−1,k) for n>0.

Arguments / value: Use n>0 and k≥0.

Example: CombinationsWithRepetition(3,2) = 6

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Complement of the magic angle
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax

Angle that adds to the magic angle to make a right angle.

Definition / convention: PI/2−MagicAngle.

Arguments / value: Stored application value: 0.6154797086703873. Radians.

Important: Stored in radians (about 35.2644 degrees). This is the finite stored binary64 approximation, not an arbitrary-precision evaluation of the defining limit, series or construction.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Supplement of the tetrahedral angle — legacy name
FunctionInfo.Description:

Angle adding to the tetrahedral angle to make a straight angle.

Definition / convention: PI−TetrahedralAngle=arccos(1/3).

Arguments / value: Stored application value: 1.2309594173407745. Radians.

Important: The identifier says complementary, but this is the SUPPLEMENT (about 70.5288 degrees), stored in radians. This is the finite stored binary64 approximation, not an arbitrary-precision evaluation of the defining limit, series or construction.

Reference: oeis.org

Photon wavelength whose quantum energy equals the electron rest energy.

Definition / convention: λC=h/(me·c).

Arguments / value: Unit: m. Stored application value: 2.4263102389E-12.

Important: This is the ordinary Compton wavelength; the reduced one is smaller by 2π. Important: The factor two represents spin degeneracy. The stored value is the application’s legacy binary64 value, not a live CODATA lookup or an uncertainty-bearing measurement. FunctionInfo.Description:

real ConicalP(integer μ, real λ, real x)
real ConicalP(real μ, real λ, real x)

A real-valued conical function whose Legendre degree has imaginary part λ.

Definition / convention: P_(−1/2+iλ)^μ(x)

Arguments / value: Real λ, x>−1. Supported μ are 0,1 and ±1/2; all other orders return NaN.

Arguments / value: Stored application value: 1.030640834100713. Dimensionless.

FunctionInfo.Title: Continuous uniform — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:

real ContinuousUniform.CDF(real lower, real upper, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. A constant density on a finite interval; equal-length subintervals have equal probabilities.

Definition / convention: f(x)=1/(upper−lower) for lower≤x≤upper, and 0 outside.

Arguments / value: Use finite lower<upper. Samples lie between the bounds; the continuous endpoint values have zero point probability.

Important: The library also accepts equal bounds as a point-mass limit. A continuous PDF is a density and can exceed one on a short interval. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one.

Example: ContinuousUniform.PDF(0,2,1) = 0.5.

Returns one random draw. A constant density on a finite interval; equal-length subintervals have equal probabilities.

Definition / convention: f(x)=1/(upper−lower) for lower≤x≤upper, and 0 outside.

Arguments / value: Use finite lower<upper. Samples lie between the bounds; the continuous endpoint values have zero point probability. rnd is a non-null System.Random instance; its state advances as draws are made.

Important: The library also accepts equal bounds as a point-mass limit. A continuous PDF is a density and can exceed one on a short interval. Sample values are random, not the density/CDF evaluated at the parameters. Reproducibility requires an explicit generator and a controlled sequence of calls; these are not cryptographic random sources.

FunctionInfo.Title: Conway–Maxwell–Poisson — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ConwayMaxwellPoisson.CDF(real lambda, real nu, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. A count distribution with dispersion controlled relative to a Poisson law.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=λ^k/((k!)^ν·Z(λ,ν)); Z(λ,ν)=Σ[j≥0] λ^j/(j!)^ν.

Arguments / value: lambda=λ>0; nu=ν≥0; k is a nonnegative integer. For ν=0, a normalizable law additionally requires λ<1.

Important: ν=1 reduces to Poisson; ν>1 usually underdisperses and 0<ν<1 overdisperses relative to it. The library parameter validator is not a convergence proof for the normalizing series; avoid the improper ν=0, λ≥1 boundary. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one. For a discrete law, the mathematical CDF is a step function over integer outcomes; use integer x at jumps. Fractional-x behavior must not be used as a continuous interpolation of probability masses.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Conway–Maxwell–Poisson — Parameter validity check
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
bool ConwayMaxwellPoisson.IsValidParameterSet(real lambda, real nu)

Returns a Boolean indicating whether the parameter set passes the library’s validity check; it does not compute a sample or a probability. A count distribution with dispersion controlled relative to a Poisson law.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=λ^k/((k!)^ν·Z(λ,ν)); Z(λ,ν)=Σ[j≥0] λ^j/(j!)^ν.

Arguments / value: lambda=λ>0; nu=ν≥0; k is a nonnegative integer. For ν=0, a normalizable law additionally requires λ<1.

Important: ν=1 reduces to Poisson; ν>1 usually underdisperses and 0<ν<1 overdisperses relative to it. The library parameter validator is not a convergence proof for the normalizing series; avoid the improper ν=0, λ≥1 boundary. This precheck is not proof of numerical convergence, finite moments, finite precision, or support of every operation. Prefer the finite, nondegenerate model conditions given here, even where the library accepts a limiting case.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Conway–Maxwell–Poisson — Probability mass P(X=k)
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ConwayMaxwellPoisson.PMF(real lambda, real nu, integer k)

Probability mass P(X=k). A count distribution with dispersion controlled relative to a Poisson law.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=λ^k/((k!)^ν·Z(λ,ν)); Z(λ,ν)=Σ[j≥0] λ^j/(j!)^ν.

Arguments / value: lambda=λ>0; nu=ν≥0; k is a nonnegative integer. For ν=0, a normalizable law additionally requires λ<1. Evaluate at integer k in the stated support.

Important: ν=1 reduces to Poisson; ν>1 usually underdisperses and 0<ν<1 overdisperses relative to it. The library parameter validator is not a convergence proof for the normalizing series; avoid the improper ν=0, λ≥1 boundary. A mass is a point probability between 0 and 1.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Conway–Maxwell–Poisson — Natural logarithm of probability mass p(x=k)
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ConwayMaxwellPoisson.PMFLn(real lambda, real nu, integer k)

Natural logarithm of probability mass p(x=k). A count distribution with dispersion controlled relative to a Poisson law.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=λ^k/((k!)^ν·Z(λ,ν)); Z(λ,ν)=Σ[j≥0] λ^j/(j!)^ν.

Arguments / value: lambda=λ>0; nu=ν≥0; k is a nonnegative integer. For ν=0, a normalizable law additionally requires λ<1. Evaluate at integer k in the stated support.

Important: ν=1 reduces to Poisson; ν>1 usually underdisperses and 0<ν<1 overdisperses relative to it. The library parameter validator is not a convergence proof for the normalizing series; avoid the improper ν=0, λ≥1 boundary. This is a natural logarithm of the mass/density, not the probability of a logarithmically transformed variable. Zero mass/density has logarithm −∞; direct log evaluation can avoid ordinary underflow.

FunctionInfo.Title: Conway look-and-say growth constant — short approximation
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ConwaysConstant

Asymptotic growth factor for the lengths of the usual look-and-say sequence.

Definition / convention: length(n+1)/length(n) → λ≈1.303577269.

Arguments / value: Stored application value: 1.30357. Dimensionless.

Important: This identifier stores only 1.30357. ConwayConstantλ3 retains a longer approximation; neither is a runtime sequence computation. This is the finite stored binary64 approximation, not an arbitrary-precision evaluation of the defining limit, series or construction.

Reference: oeis.org

FunctionInfo.Title: Regular Coulomb-wave normalization
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real CoulombC(integer L, real η)

The small-radius normalization factor of the regular Coulomb solution.

Definition / convention: C_L(η)=2ᴸ exp(−PI·η/2)|Γ(L+1+iη)|/Γ(2L+2); F_L(η,ρ) ~ C_L(η)ρ^(L+1).

Arguments / value: Integer L≥0; real Sommerfeld parameter η.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: regular Coulomb wave
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real CoulombF(integer L, real η, real ρ)

A real solution of the radial Coulomb scattering equation.

Definition / convention: u″+[1−2η/ρ−L(L+1)/ρ²]u=0; F_L(η,ρ)

Arguments / value: Integer L≥0, real η; use ρ>0. F is regular at the origin; G is the independent irregular solution.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Derivative of regular Coulomb wave
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real CoulombFprime(integer L, real η, real ρ)

A real solution of the radial Coulomb scattering equation differentiated in its radial argument.

Definition / convention: u″+[1−2η/ρ−L(L+1)/ρ²]u=0; F_L′(η,ρ)

Arguments / value: Integer L≥0, real η; use ρ>0. F is regular at the origin; G is the independent irregular solution.

Important: Derivatives are with respect to dimensionless ρ, not energy or physical radius. Returned GSL overflow scaling exponents are not applied; avoid interpreting a scaled-overflow result as the full derivative.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: irregular Coulomb wave
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real CoulombG(integer L, real η, real ρ)

A real solution of the radial Coulomb scattering equation.

Definition / convention: u″+[1−2η/ρ−L(L+1)/ρ²]u=0; G_L(η,ρ)

Arguments / value: Integer L≥0, real η; use ρ>0. F is regular at the origin; G is the independent irregular solution.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Derivative of irregular Coulomb wave
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real CoulombGprime(integer L, real η, real ρ)

A real solution of the radial Coulomb scattering equation differentiated in its radial argument.

Definition / convention: u″+[1−2η/ρ−L(L+1)/ρ²]u=0; G_L′(η,ρ)

Arguments / value: Integer L≥0, real η; use ρ>0. F is regular at the origin; G is the independent irregular solution.

Important: Derivatives are with respect to dimensionless ρ, not energy or physical radius. Current forwarding uses gsl_sf_coulomb_wave_FG_e(η,ρ,L,L,...), whose G output has order L−L=0. For L≠0 this wrapper therefore returns G′₀, not the advertised G′_L. Scaling exponents returned by GSL are not applied.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Application-defined Coulomb linear combination
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real CoulombW(integer L, real η, real ρ)

Combines the regular and irregular Coulomb waves using the application’s fixed order-1 and order-2 normalization coefficients.

Definition / convention: CoulombW(L,η,ρ)=C₁(η)F_L(η,ρ)+C₂(η)G_L(η,ρ)

Arguments / value: Integer L≥0, real η and ρ>0 for the nonsingular irregular term.

Important: Despite the W name this is not the Wronskian, a Whittaker W function, or a boundary-condition-independent “complete” physical solution.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Wigner 3-j symbol
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Coupling3j(real j1, real j2, real j3, real m1, real m2, real m3)

An angular-momentum recoupling coefficient with phase and selection rules fixed by the conventional Wigner/Racah definition.

Arguments / value: Arguments are the actual nonnegative integer or half-integer spin values. Magnetic projections must obey |m|≤j, compatible parity and m₁+m₂+m₃=0.

Important: The integer and real 3-j/6-j overloads use DIFFERENT argument units; explicitly use real literals when supplying actual spins.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Wigner 3-j symbol
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Coupling3j(integer ja, integer jb, integer jc, integer ma, integer mb, integer mc)

An angular-momentum recoupling coefficient with phase and selection rules fixed by the conventional Wigner/Racah definition.

Arguments / value: Every integer argument is TWICE the physical spin/projection: e.g. 1 represents 1/2. Magnetic projections must obey |m|≤j, compatible parity and m₁+m₂+m₃=0.

Important: The integer and real 3-j/6-j overloads use DIFFERENT argument units; explicitly use real literals when supplying actual spins.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Wigner 6-j symbol
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Coupling6j(real j1, real j2, real j3, real j4, real j5, real j6)

An angular-momentum recoupling coefficient with phase and selection rules fixed by the conventional Wigner/Racah definition.

Arguments / value: Arguments are the actual nonnegative integer or half-integer spin values. Triangle and parity selection rules apply; forbidden couplings vanish or are rejected by the library.

Important: The integer and real 3-j/6-j overloads use DIFFERENT argument units; explicitly use real literals when supplying actual spins.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Wigner 6-j symbol
FunctionInfo.Description:

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Wigner 9-j symbol
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Coupling9j(integer ja, integer jb, integer jc, integer jd, integer je, integer jf, integer jg, integer jh, integer ji)

An angular-momentum recoupling coefficient with phase and selection rules fixed by the conventional Wigner/Racah definition.

Definition / convention: Arguments specify the successive rows of the 3×3 Wigner array.

Arguments / value: Every integer argument is TWICE the physical spin/projection: e.g. 1 represents 1/2. Triangle and parity selection rules apply; forbidden couplings vanish or are rejected by the library.

Important: Current implementation forwards jf as the ninth argument instead of ji. Thus changing ji alone does not change the result; it is not a general 9-j calculation until that wrapper is corrected.

FunctionInfo.Title: Copper X unit
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real CuXUnit

Historical X-ray length unit tied to the Cu Kα₁ line.

Definition / convention: λ(Cu Kα₁)=1537.400 xu(Cu).

Arguments / value: Unit: m. Stored application value: 1.00207697E-13.

Important: Not the same calibrated unit as the molybdenum X unit. The stored value is the application’s legacy binary64 value, not a live CODATA lookup or an uncertainty-bearing measurement. Use the cited current NIST/SI definition for precision work; independently stored related constants may not be numerically consistent.

Reference: physics.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Cylindrical regular conical function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real CylindricalConicalP(integer m, real λ, real x)

A negative-order conical Legendre function used in separated coordinate problems.

Definition / convention: P_(−1/2+iλ)^(−m)(x)

Arguments / value: Integer m≥−1, real λ and x>−1; this wrapper additionally rejects x=0.

Important: The index determines the negative order; it is not the μ argument of ConicalP.

Reference: www.gnu.org

FunctionInfo.Title: Dawson integral
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Dawson(real x)

An exponentially scaled integral of exp(t²), often encountered in Gaussian line-shape calculations.

Definition / convention: D(x)=exp(−x²)∫₀ˣ exp(t²) dt

Arguments / value: Real x. It is odd, D(0)=0, and D(x) is asymptotic to 1/(2x) for large |x|.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Normalized Debye integral
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Debye(integer n, real x)

A thermal integral used in lattice heat-capacity and related statistical-physics models.

Definition / convention: Dₙ(x)=n/xⁿ ∫₀ˣ tⁿ/(exp(t)−1) dt; Dₙ(0)=1 for n>0.

Arguments / value: Use integer n=1,…,6 and x≥0 for the supported normalized functions.

Important: Legacy behavior outside these orders is NOT the same definition: n=0 returns 0, and for other n with x>9 the wrapper returns Γ(n+1)ζ(n+1), omitting n/xⁿ. Do not use that fallback as a normalized higher-order Debye function.

Example: Debye(1,0) = 1

Reference: www.gnu.org

FunctionInfo.Title: Delian constant
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real DelianConstant

Factor by which a cube’s edge must grow to double its volume.

Definition / convention: ∛2.

Arguments / value: Stored application value: 1.2599210498948732. Dimensionless.

Important: A geometric scale factor, not twice the original edge length. This is the finite stored binary64 approximation, not an arbitrary-precision evaluation of the defining limit, series or construction.

Reference: oeis.org

FunctionInfo.Title: Centered five-point difference
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Derivative.centeredFivePointMethod(function fx, real x, natural order, real eps)

A finite-difference derivative estimate, recursively extended to higher orders.

Definition / convention: [f(x−2h)−8f(x−h)+8f(x+h)−f(x+2h)]/(12h) for order=1.

Arguments / value: Nonnegative integer order; order zero returns fx(x). Step h=x·eps; when it is zero the wrapper substitutes 1e−25.

Important: eps is a step-size parameter, not a guaranteed result error. Extremely small steps lose subtraction accuracy. In recursive higher-order calls this implementation does not forward the chosen eps, so inner levels use their default. Prefer the Math.NET derivative entry when appropriate.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Numerical derivative at a point
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Derivative.derivative(function fx, real x, natural order)

Uses Math.NET’s finite-difference derivative implementation.

Definition / convention: d^order fx(x)/dx^order

Arguments / value: Nonnegative integer order; order zero returns the original function value.

Important: Step selection is delegated to Math.NET; high orders can be sensitive to roundoff and nonsmooth inputs.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Select a numerical derivative method
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Derivative.derivative(string methodName, function fx, real x, natural order, real eps)

Dispatches to an existing finite-difference or Math.NET derivative implementation.

Definition / convention: Estimate d^order fx(x)/dx^order.

Arguments / value: fx is a real callable; x the evaluation point; order is a nonnegative integer; eps>0 controls the hand-written steps.

Important: Exact names: centered order-point method; finite difference formula; stable finite difference formula; two-point finite difference formula; centered five-point method. Unknown names return NaN. The centered order-point method delegates to Math.NET and ignores eps.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Derivative as a callable
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
function Derivative.derivativeAsFunction(function fx, real x, natural order)

Builds a real callable evaluating the order-th derivative at its own argument.

Definition / convention: g(t)=d^order fx(t)/dt^order

Arguments / value: Nonnegative integer order; order zero returns the original function itself.

Important: The x parameter is ignored: the RETURNED function’s argument selects the evaluation point.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Numerical derivative at a point

Uses Math.NET’s finite-difference derivative implementation.

Definition / convention: d^order fx(x)/dx^order

Arguments / value: Nonnegative integer order; order zero returns the original function value.

Important: The eps parameter is ignored by derivativeAtPoint; the Math.NET step selection is used.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Forward finite difference
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Derivative.finiteDifferenceFormula(function fx, real x, natural order, real eps)

A finite-difference derivative estimate, recursively extended to higher orders.

Definition / convention: [f(x+h)−f(x)]/h for order=1.

Arguments / value: Nonnegative integer order; order zero returns fx(x). Step h=x·eps; when it is zero the wrapper substitutes 1e−25.

Important: eps is a step-size parameter, not a guaranteed result error. Extremely small steps lose subtraction accuracy. In recursive higher-order calls this implementation does not forward the chosen eps, so inner levels use their default. Prefer the Math.NET derivative entry when appropriate.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Representable-step forward difference
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Derivative.stableFiniteDifferenceFormula(function fx, real x, natural order, real eps)

A finite-difference derivative estimate, recursively extended to higher orders.

Definition / convention: [f(x+h)−f(x)]/((x+h)−x) for order=1.

Arguments / value: Nonnegative integer order; order zero returns fx(x). Step begins at sqrt(eps)·x and uses the actual representable difference; at zero a fixed tiny fallback is used.

Important: eps is a step-size parameter, not a guaranteed result error. Extremely small steps lose subtraction accuracy. In recursive higher-order calls this implementation does not forward the chosen eps, so inner levels use their default. Prefer the Math.NET derivative entry when appropriate.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Centered two-point difference
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Derivative.twoPointfiniteDifferenceFormula(function fx, real x, natural order, real eps)

A finite-difference derivative estimate, recursively extended to higher orders.

Definition / convention: [f(x+h)−f(x−h)]/(2h) for order=1.

Arguments / value: Nonnegative integer order; order zero returns fx(x). Step h=x·eps; when it is zero the wrapper substitutes 1e−25.

Important: eps is a step-size parameter, not a guaranteed result error. Extremely small steps lose subtraction accuracy. In recursive higher-order calls this implementation does not forward the chosen eps, so inner levels use their default. Prefer the Math.NET derivative entry when appropriate.

FunctionInfo.Title: Dirichlet — Parameter validity check
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
bool Dirichlet.IsValidParameterSet(Double[] alpha)

Returns a Boolean indicating whether the parameter set passes the library’s validity check; it does not compute a sample or a probability. A joint distribution over probability vectors, often used as a prior on categorical proportions.

Definition / convention: f(x)=Γ(Σαᵢ)/ΠΓ(αᵢ) · Πxᵢ^(αᵢ−1), with Σxᵢ=1.

Arguments / value: alpha contains positive finite concentration parameters. The returned array has the same dimension, nonnegative components and sum approximately one.

Important: The ordinary density is on the simplex, not all of Euclidean space. A unit concentration vector gives a uniform simplex distribution; library-accepted degenerate parameters need separate care. This precheck is not proof of numerical convergence, finite moments, finite precision, or support of every operation. Prefer the finite, nondegenerate model conditions given here, even where the library accepts a limiting case.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax

Returns one random draw. A joint distribution over probability vectors, often used as a prior on categorical proportions.

Definition / convention: f(x)=Γ(Σαᵢ)/ΠΓ(αᵢ) · Πxᵢ^(αᵢ−1), with Σxᵢ=1.

Arguments / value: alpha contains positive finite concentration parameters. The returned array has the same dimension, nonnegative components and sum approximately one. rnd is a non-null System.Random instance; its state advances as draws are made.

Important: The ordinary density is on the simplex, not all of Euclidean space. A unit concentration vector gives a uniform simplex distribution; library-accepted degenerate parameters need separate care. Sample values are random, not the density/CDF evaluated at the parameters. Reproducibility requires an explicit generator and a controlled sequence of calls; these are not cryptographic random sources.

FunctionInfo.Title: Discrete uniform — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real DiscreteUniform.CDF(integer lower, integer upper, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. An equally likely INTEGER from an inclusive integer interval.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=1/(upper−lower+1), k=lower,…,upper.

Arguments / value: lower and upper are integers with lower≤upper. Both endpoints belong to the support.

Important: Unlike typical Random.Next bounds, this distribution includes the upper endpoint. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one. For a discrete law, the mathematical CDF is a step function over integer outcomes; use integer x at jumps. Fractional-x behavior must not be used as a continuous interpolation of probability masses.

Example: DiscreteUniform.PMF(1,6,6) = 1/6.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Erlang — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Erlang.CDF(integer shape, real rate, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. An integer-shape gamma distribution: the waiting time for shape events in a Poisson process of the given rate.

Definition / convention: f(x)=rate^shape · x^(shape−1)·exp(−rate·x)/Γ(shape); E[X]=shape/rate.

Arguments / value: shape is a positive integer; rate>0; x≥0. Scale is 1/rate.

Important: The ordinary law needs positive shape and rate; the library additionally supports limiting parameter cases. Do not confuse its rate argument with a scale. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Description:

FunctionInfo.Description:

Constant difference between the harmonic sum and the natural logarithm in the large-n limit.

Definition / convention: γ=lim(n→∞)[Σ(k=1..n)1/k−ln(n)].

FunctionInfo.Title: Euler totient
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Eulerφ(integer n)

Counts integers from 1 through n that are coprime to n.

Definition / convention: φ(n)=n·∏(1−1/p), over distinct primes p dividing n.

Arguments / value: Positive integer n; φ(1)=1. Inputs below 1 return NaN.

Important: The current implementation allocates a sieve of size proportional to n; this is not appropriate for very large integers.

Example: Eulerφ(9) = 6

Eigenvalue decomposition.

Definition / convention: A·V≈V·D

FunctionInfo.Title: Exponential — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Exponential.CDF(real rate, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. The nonnegative, memoryless waiting time to the next event in a constant-rate Poisson process.

Definition / convention: f(x)=rate·exp(−rate·x); F(x)=1−exp(−rate·x); E[X]=1/rate.

Arguments / value: rate>0 and x≥0; rate is inverse mean waiting time, not the mean or scale.

Important: This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one.

Example: Exponential.CDF(1,1) = 1−exp(−1).

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Exponential — Inverse CDF (quantile)
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax

Maps cumulative probability to the corresponding outcome threshold. The nonnegative, memoryless waiting time to the next event in a constant-rate Poisson process.

Definition / convention: f(x)=rate·exp(−rate·x); F(x)=1−exp(−rate·x); E[X]=1/rate.

Arguments / value: rate>0 and x≥0; rate is inverse mean waiting time, not the mean or scale. The argument p/probability is a cumulative probability in [0,1], not another shape parameter.

Important: Interior probabilities 0<p<1 avoid infinite endpoints for unbounded distributions. Numerical inversion has finite accuracy.

Example: Exponential.CDF(1,1) = 1−exp(−1).

FunctionInfo.Title: Normalized Fermi–Dirac integral, order 0
FunctionInfo.Description:

The Fermi occupation integral with the gamma normalization included.

Arguments / value: x is real and dimensionless. This entry fixes j=0.

Important: Some references omit 1/Γ(j+1); their values then differ by that factor.

Example: FermiDiracF0(0) ≈ ln(2)

Important: This is a tail integral, not the integral from zero to b.

FunctionInfo.Title: Fisher–Snedecor F — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FisherSnedecor.CDF(real d1, real d2, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. The ratio of two independent chi-squared variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom.

Definition / convention: X=(U/d1)/(V/d2), U~χ²(d1), V~χ²(d2).

Arguments / value: d1>0 and d2>0 are numerator and denominator degrees of freedom, respectively; x≥0.

Important: The mean exists only for d2>2; the variance needs d2>4. Exchanging d1 and d2 describes the reciprocal variable, not the same law. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Fisher–Snedecor F — Inverse CDF (quantile)
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FisherSnedecor.InvCDF(real d1, real d2, real p)

Maps cumulative probability to the corresponding outcome threshold. The ratio of two independent chi-squared variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom.

Definition / convention: X=(U/d1)/(V/d2), U~χ²(d1), V~χ²(d2).

Arguments / value: d1>0 and d2>0 are numerator and denominator degrees of freedom, respectively; x≥0. The argument p/probability is a cumulative probability in [0,1], not another shape parameter.

Important: The mean exists only for d2>2; the variance needs d2>4. Exchanging d1 and d2 describes the reciprocal variable, not the same law. Interior probabilities 0<p<1 avoid infinite endpoints for unbounded distributions. Numerical inversion has finite accuracy.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Fisher–Snedecor F — Parameter validity check
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
bool FisherSnedecor.IsValidParameterSet(real d1, real d2)

Returns a Boolean indicating whether the parameter set passes the library’s validity check; it does not compute a sample or a probability. The ratio of two independent chi-squared variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom.

Definition / convention: X=(U/d1)/(V/d2), U~χ²(d1), V~χ²(d2).

Arguments / value: d1>0 and d2>0 are numerator and denominator degrees of freedom, respectively; x≥0.

Important: The mean exists only for d2>2; the variance needs d2>4. Exchanging d1 and d2 describes the reciprocal variable, not the same law. This precheck is not proof of numerical convergence, finite moments, finite precision, or support of every operation. Prefer the finite, nondegenerate model conditions given here, even where the library accepts a limiting case.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Fisher–Snedecor F — Probability density f(x)
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FisherSnedecor.PDF(real d1, real d2, real x)

Probability density f(x). The ratio of two independent chi-squared variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom.

Definition / convention: X=(U/d1)/(V/d2), U~χ²(d1), V~χ²(d2).

Arguments / value: d1>0 and d2>0 are numerator and denominator degrees of freedom, respectively; x≥0. Evaluate at x; the support is specified above.

Important: The mean exists only for d2>2; the variance needs d2>4. Exchanging d1 and d2 describes the reciprocal variable, not the same law. A density is not P(X=x): point probability is zero for a continuous law. Integrate the density over an interval to obtain a probability.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Fisher–Snedecor F — Natural logarithm of probability density f(x)
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FisherSnedecor.PDFLn(real d1, real d2, real x)

Natural logarithm of probability density f(x). The ratio of two independent chi-squared variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom.

Definition / convention: X=(U/d1)/(V/d2), U~χ²(d1), V~χ²(d2).

Arguments / value: d1>0 and d2>0 are numerator and denominator degrees of freedom, respectively; x≥0. Evaluate at x; the support is specified above.

Important: The mean exists only for d2>2; the variance needs d2>4. Exchanging d1 and d2 describes the reciprocal variable, not the same law. This is a natural logarithm of the mass/density, not the probability of a logarithmically transformed variable. Zero mass/density has logarithm −∞; direct log evaluation can avoid ordinary underflow.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Fisher–Snedecor F — One random draw
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax

Returns one random draw. The ratio of two independent chi-squared variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom.

Definition / convention: X=(U/d1)/(V/d2), U~χ²(d1), V~χ²(d2).

Arguments / value: d1>0 and d2>0 are numerator and denominator degrees of freedom, respectively; x≥0. Uses the library’s default random source; no explicit seed is accepted by this overload.

Important: The mean exists only for d2>2; the variance needs d2>4. Exchanging d1 and d2 describes the reciprocal variable, not the same law. Sample values are random, not the density/CDF evaluated at the parameters. Reproducibility requires an explicit generator and a controlled sequence of calls; these are not cryptographic random sources.

FunctionInfo.Title: Fransén–Robinson constant
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FransénRobinsonConstant

Integral of the reciprocal gamma function over the nonnegative real axis.

Definition / convention: F=∫₀∞ 1/Γ(x) dx.

Arguments / value: Stored application value: 2.8077702420285195. Dimensionless.

Important: The reciprocal gamma function tends to zero at x=0, so the endpoint is interpreted continuously. This is the finite stored binary64 approximation, not an arbitrary-precision evaluation of the defining limit, series or construction.

Reference: oeis.org

FunctionInfo.Title: Complex Fresnel integral
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
complex Fresnel(real x)

Combines the Fresnel cosine and sine integrals into one complex result.

Definition / convention: F(x)=C(x)+iS(x)=∫₀ˣ exp(i·PI·t²/2) dt

Arguments / value: The argument x is real; the result is complex. Both component integrals are zero at the origin.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Fresnel cosine integral
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FresnelC(real x)

The real component of the normalized Fresnel integral, used in diffraction.

Definition / convention: C(x)=∫₀ˣ cos(PI·t²/2) dt

Arguments / value: Real x. The PI/2 factor is part of this convention; C tends to 1/2 as x→+∞.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Fresnel sine integral
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FresnelS(real x)

The imaginary component of the normalized Fresnel integral, used in diffraction.

Definition / convention: S(x)=∫₀ˣ sin(PI·t²/2) dt

Arguments / value: Real x. The PI/2 factor is part of this convention; S tends to 1/2 as x→+∞.

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Brent bracketed root finder
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FunctionRoot.BrentMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real errorMax, natural N)

Combines bracketing, interpolation and bisection to find a real zero.

Definition / convention: fx(root) ≈ 0.

Arguments / value: errorMax>0 is the requested solver accuracy; N>0 limits iterations (default 10,000).

Important: Use a continuous fx and a<b with opposite endpoint signs. Returns NaN when TryFindRoot fails. Repeated roots, discontinuities and nonfinite evaluations may defeat convergence.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: One-variable Broyden wrapper
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FunctionRoot.BroydenMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real errorMax, natural N)

Applies the multidimensional Broyden solver to a one-element system.

Definition / convention: fx(root) ≈ 0.

Arguments / value: errorMax>0 is the requested solver accuracy; N>0 limits iterations (default 10,000).

Important: Only the midpoint (a+b)/2 is used as the starting guess; a,b are NOT enforced bounds or a guaranteed bracket. TryFindRoot failure returns NaN. Repeated roots, discontinuities and nonfinite evaluations may defeat convergence.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Bisection root finder
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FunctionRoot.bisectionMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real errorMax, natural N)

Repeatedly halves an interval while retaining a sign-changing bracket.

Definition / convention: fx(root) ≈ 0.

Arguments / value: errorMax>0 is the requested solver accuracy; N>0 limits iterations (default 10,000).

Important: Use a continuous fx and a<b bracketing a root. It converges predictably but usually more slowly than Brent; TryFindRoot failure returns NaN. Repeated roots, discontinuities and nonfinite evaluations may defeat convergence.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Select a numerical root method
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FunctionRoot.findRoot(string methodName, function fx, real a, real b, real errorMax, natural N)

Dispatches a real equation fx(x)=0 to a named root-finding algorithm.

Definition / convention: Find x such that fx(x)=0.

Arguments / value: Positive errorMax and positive iteration count N, in the supported integer range; callable fx must return meaningful finite values near the root.

Important: Exact names: bisection method; secant method; secant Newton Raphson method; Brent's method; Broyden's method. Unknown names return NaN. The interpretation of a,b and of errorMax depends on the algorithm; it is not a universal certified root-error bound.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Secant root finder
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FunctionRoot.secantMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real errorMax, natural N)

Uses the line through the two most recent function values to estimate the next root.

Definition / convention: fx(root) ≈ 0.

Arguments / value: errorMax>0 is the requested solver accuracy; N>0 limits iterations (default 10,000).

Important: a,b are initial guesses, not enforced bounds. Iteration can leave the interval. This implementation returns a value only if |fx(result)|≤errorMax after its loop; otherwise NaN. Repeated roots, discontinuities and nonfinite evaluations may defeat convergence.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Bounded secant convenience wrapper
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real FunctionRoot.secantNewtonRaphsonMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real errorMax, natural N)

Uses Math.NET’s secant method without an analytic derivative.

Definition / convention: fx(root) ≈ 0.

Arguments / value: errorMax>0 is the requested solver accuracy; N>0 limits iterations (default 10,000).

Important: The initial guesses are (a+b)/2 and (a+b)/3, and [a,b] is supplied as the interval. Despite the name this is not a Newton step using an exact derivative. Degenerate initial guesses can fail. Repeated roots, discontinuities and nonfinite evaluations may defeat convergence.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real G

Sets the strength of Newtonian gravitational attraction.

Definition / convention: F=G·m₁·m₂/r².

Arguments / value: Unit: m³ kg⁻¹ s⁻². Stored application value: 6.673848E-11.

Important: The short name G and NewtonianConstantOfGravitation have slightly different stored values. G is experimentally determined, not an SI defining constant. The stored value is the application’s legacy binary64 value, not a live CODATA lookup or an uncertainty-bearing measurement. Use the cited current NIST/SI definition for precision work; independently stored related constants may not be numerically consistent.

Reference: physics.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: One-dimensional Gabor function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Gabor(real x, real mean, real amplitude, real position, real width, real phase, real frequency)

A localized sinusoidal signal with a Gaussian envelope and an additive mean.

Definition / convention: Gaussian-windowed cosine with the supplied amplitude, position, width, phase and frequency.

Arguments / value: x is the evaluation coordinate; mean is the offset, position the envelope center, width its positive scale, amplitude its height. Frequency and phase follow Accord’s Function1D convention.

Important: This returns a real scalar. It is distinct from the wavelength/rotation-based complex two-dimensional overload.

Reference: accord-framework.net

FunctionInfo.Title: Two-dimensional complex Gabor kernel
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
complex Gabor(complex z, real λ, real θ, real ψ, real σ, real γ)

A rotated anisotropic Gaussian envelope multiplied by a complex sinusoid.

Definition / convention: exp[−(x′²+γ²y′²)/(2σ²)]·exp[i(2PI·x′/λ+ψ)]

Arguments / value: x′=xcosθ+ysinθ, y′=−xsinθ+ycosθ; θ,ψ are radians, λ is wavelength, σ>0 the envelope width and γ the aspect ratio.

Important: This wrapper takes x=Re(z), y=Im(z) but casts both to integers before calling Accord. Noninteger coordinates are truncated, not sampled continuously.

Reference: accord-framework.net

FunctionInfo.Title: Gamma distribution — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Gamma.CDF(real shape, real rate, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. A nonnegative waiting-time/scale model with a positive shape parameter, extending Erlang to noninteger shapes.

Definition / convention: f(x)=rate^shape · x^(shape−1)·exp(−rate·x)/Γ(shape); Var[X]=shape/rate².

Arguments / value: shape>0, rate>0, x≥0; the scale is 1/rate.

Important: This class uses SHAPE/RATE for its ordinary static functions. Library limiting cases at zero/infinite parameters are not the ordinary finite positive-parameter density. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one.

Example: Gamma.PDF(1,2,0.5) = 2·exp(−1).

FunctionInfo.Title: Geometric — trials until success — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Geometric.CDF(real p, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. The number of Bernoulli trials up to and INCLUDING the first success.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=p(1−p)^(k−1), k=1,2,…; E[X]=1/p.

Arguments / value: Use 0<p≤1 for a proper finite waiting-time law. This implementation never samples zero.

Important: This is NOT the alternative failures-before-success convention on 0,1,… . The parameter validator accepts p=0, but that boundary has no finite first-success time. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one. For a discrete law, the mathematical CDF is a step function over integer outcomes; use integer x at jumps. Fractional-x behavior must not be used as a continuous interpolation of probability masses.

Example: Geometric.PMF(0.5,1) = 0.5; the smallest possible sample is 1.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

Important: This is NOT the alternative failures-before-success convention on 0,1,… . The parameter validator accepts p=0, but that boundary has no finite first-success time. This precheck is not proof of numerical convergence, finite moments, finite precision, or support of every operation. Prefer the finite, nondegenerate model conditions given here, even where the library accepts a limiting case.

FunctionInfo.Title: Hypergeometric — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Hypergeometric.CDF(integer population, integer success, integer draws, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. The number of successes in draws without replacement from a finite population.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=C(success,k)·C(population−success,draws−k)/C(population,draws).

Arguments / value: population, success and draws are integers; 0≤success≤population and 0≤draws≤population. Support: max(0,draws−population+success)≤k≤min(draws,success).

Important: Sampling is without replacement, unlike the independent-trial Binomial model. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one. For a discrete law, the mathematical CDF is a step function over integer outcomes; use integer x at jumps. Fractional-x behavior must not be used as a continuous interpolation of probability masses.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Hypergeometric — Parameter validity check
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
bool Hypergeometric.IsValidParameterSet(integer population, integer success, integer draws)

Returns a Boolean indicating whether the parameter set passes the library’s validity check; it does not compute a sample or a probability. The number of successes in draws without replacement from a finite population.

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=C(success,k)·C(population−success,draws−k)/C(population,draws).

Arguments / value: population, success and draws are integers; 0≤success≤population and 0≤draws≤population. Support: max(0,draws−population+success)≤k≤min(draws,success).

Important: Sampling is without replacement, unlike the independent-trial Binomial model. This precheck is not proof of numerical convergence, finite moments, finite precision, or support of every operation. Prefer the finite, nondegenerate model conditions given here, even where the library accepts a limiting case.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Hypergeometric — One random draw

Definition / convention: P(X=k)=C(success,k)·C(population−success,draws−k)/C(population,draws).

Arguments / value: population, success and draws are integers; 0≤success≤population and 0≤draws≤population. Support: max(0,draws−population+success)≤k≤min(draws,success). Uses the library’s default random source; no explicit seed is accepted by this overload.

FunctionInfo.Title: Confluent hypergeometric limit function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Hypergeometric0F1(real c, real x)

A hypergeometric function closely related to Bessel functions.

Definition / convention: ₀F₁(;c;x)=Σₖ₌₀^∞ xᵏ/[(c)ₖ k!]

Arguments / value: Real c,x; c must not be zero or a negative integer for the ordinary definition.

Important: The empty numerator parameter list is intentional. The Pochhammer symbol denotes a rising factorial.

Example: Hypergeometric0F1(1,0) = 1

FunctionInfo.Title: Kummer confluent hypergeometric function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Hypergeometric1F1(real a, real b, real x)

The regular confluent hypergeometric solution M(a,b,x).

Definition / convention: ₁F₁(a;b;x)=Σₖ₌₀^∞ (a)ₖ xᵏ/[(b)ₖ k!]

Arguments / value: The integer m,n overload uses m as a and n as b. Real x; ordinary denominator parameters b=0,−1,… are singular except for valid terminating/limiting cases.

Important: Unlike the similarly named Tricomi U, this is the solution normalized to 1 at x=0.

Example: Hypergeometric1F1(1.0,1.0,1) ≈ e

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Asymptotic hypergeometric function ₂F₀
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Hypergeometric2F0(real a, real b, real x)

A generally divergent hypergeometric series interpreted through a confluent-hypergeometric continuation.

Definition / convention: ₂F₀(a,b;;x) ~ Σₖ₌₀^∞ (a)ₖ(b)ₖ xᵏ/k!

Arguments / value: For ordinary nonterminating parameters the series is asymptotic, not a convergent power series at nonzero x. GSL provides the real x<0 branch via U.

Important: The series terminates when a or b is a nonpositive integer. Do not label this the Gauss ₂F₁ function.

Reference: www.gnu.org

FunctionInfo.Title: Gauss hypergeometric function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Hypergeometric2F1(real a, real b, real c, real x)

The Gauss hypergeometric solution with numerator parameters a,b and denominator parameter c.

Definition / convention: ₂F₁(a,b;c;x)=Σₖ₌₀^∞ (a)ₖ(b)ₖ xᵏ/[(c)ₖ k!].

Arguments / value: Real x in the GSL real-domain implementation; the series converges for |x|<1, with supported boundary/continuation cases. The ordinary form has denominator poles at c=0,−1,−2,… unless a limiting cancellation applies.

Important: Do not infer complex branch values for x>1 from this real-valued interface.

Reference: www.gnu.org

Arguments / value: The complex overload supplies b=conjugate(a), not an arbitrary second complex parameter. Real x in the GSL real-domain implementation; the series converges for |x|<1, with supported boundary/continuation cases. The ordinary form has denominator poles at c=0,−1,−2,… unless a limiting cancellation applies.

Definition / convention: ₂F₁(a,b;c;x)=Σₖ₌₀^∞ (a)ₖ(b)ₖ xᵏ/[(c)ₖ k!] ; returned value is ₂F₁/Γ(c).

FunctionInfo.Title: Double-exponential quadrature
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Integral.doubleExponentialTransformation(function fx, real a, real b, real N)

Transforms a finite-interval integral to rapidly decaying tails, often useful for endpoint singularities.

Arguments / value: fx is a real-valued callable. Supply integral N>0 and a<b, except supported infinite endpoints of the adaptive method.

Important: The wrapper passes target relative error 1/N to Math.NET, not a literal number of samples. Endpoint behavior and finite precision still limit attainable accuracy. These are numerical estimates, not symbolic antiderivatives or certified error bounds.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Adaptive Gauss–Kronrod quadrature
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Integral.infiniteAdaptiveGaussKronrodMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real N)

Adaptively subdivides the integral using Gauss–Kronrod estimates; the Accord algorithm also supports transformed infinite intervals.

Arguments / value: fx is a real-valued callable. Supply integral N>0 and a<b, except supported infinite endpoints of the adaptive method.

Important: N configures the Accord integration workspace/subinterval limit, not an exact number of function calls. Uses library default tolerances; returns NaN when Compute reports failure. These are numerical estimates, not symbolic antiderivatives or certified error bounds.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Select a numerical integration method
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Integral.integrate(string methodName, function fx, real a, real b, integer N)

Dispatches to one of the existing scalar quadrature implementations.

Definition / convention: Approximates ∫ₐᵇ fx(t) dt.

Arguments / value: Supply a real callable fx, a<b and an appropriate positive integral N.

Important: Exact method names: trapezoidal method; rectangle method; Simpson's method; double exponential transformation; non-adaptive Gauss–Kronrod method; infinity-adaptive Gauss–Kronrod method; Monte Carlo method; Romberg's method. Unknown names return NaN. N means panels, tolerance inverse or depth depending on the selected method; the default 10,000 is invalid for Romberg.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Monte Carlo quadrature
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Integral.monteCarloMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real N)

Estimates a one-dimensional integral by random sampling over its interval.

Definition / convention: Integral estimate ≈ (b−a)·sample mean of f(U), U uniform on [a,b].

Arguments / value: fx is a real-valued callable. Supply integral N>0 and a<b, except supported infinite endpoints of the adaptive method.

Important: N is the sample count, cast to an integer. Sampling error is stochastic, usually proportional to 1/sqrt(N), not a guaranteed deterministic tolerance. These are numerical estimates, not symbolic antiderivatives or certified error bounds.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Nonadaptive Gauss–Kronrod quadrature
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Integral.nonAdaptiveGaussKronrodMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real N)

Uses embedded quadrature rules and their difference as an error estimate without adaptive interval subdivision.

Arguments / value: fx is a real-valued callable. Supply integral N>0 and a<b, except supported infinite endpoints of the adaptive method.

Important: The wrapper passes 1/N as the library tolerance, NOT N as a panel count. Use finite N>0; nonsmooth or singular integrands may not meet the requested accuracy. These are numerical estimates, not symbolic antiderivatives or certified error bounds.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Composite midpoint rule
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Integral.rectangleMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real N)

Approximates area by equal-width rectangles evaluated at their midpoints.

Definition / convention: h·Σⱼ₌₀ᴺ⁻¹ f(a+(j+1/2)h), h=(b−a)/N.

Arguments / value: fx is a real-valued callable. Supply integral N>0 and finite bounds a,b in either order.

Important: N is the number of panels. For smooth f, error is generally of order h². A signed step (b−a)/N follows the interval from a to b. Reversing the limits reverses the integral sign; equal bounds give zero for a finite integrand. These are numerical estimates, not symbolic antiderivatives or certified error bounds.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Romberg extrapolation
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Integral.rombergMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real N)

Extrapolates a sequence of trapezoidal estimates toward zero mesh spacing.

Definition / convention: Richardson extrapolation cancels successive even powers of the panel width.

Arguments / value: fx is a real-valued callable. Supply integral N>0 and a<b, except supported infinite endpoints of the adaptive method.

Important: N is the integer extrapolation depth, not the panel count; default 6 and N>30 is explicitly rejected. Work grows rapidly with depth. These are numerical estimates, not symbolic antiderivatives or certified error bounds.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Composite Simpson rule
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Integral.simpsonMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real N)

Integrates piecewise quadratic interpolation on pairs of equal-width panels.

Definition / convention: h/3·[f(a)+4f(a+h)+2f(a+2h)+…+4f(b−h)+f(b)].

Arguments / value: fx is a real-valued callable. Supply integral N>0 and finite bounds a,b in either order.

Important: Use a positive even integer N. This wrapper increments odd N by 1; it does not interpret fractional N consistently. Smooth-function error is generally of order h⁴. A signed step (b−a)/N follows the interval from a to b. Reversing the limits reverses the integral sign; equal bounds give zero for a finite integrand. These are numerical estimates, not symbolic antiderivatives or certified error bounds.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Composite trapezoidal rule
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Integral.trapezoidalMethod(function fx, real a, real b, real N)

Approximates the integral by straight-line interpolation on each panel.

Definition / convention: h·[f(a)/2+Σⱼ₌₁ᴺ⁻¹ f(a+jh)+f(b)/2], h=(b−a)/N.

Arguments / value: fx is a real-valued callable. Supply integral N>0 and finite bounds a,b in either order.

Important: N is the number of panels; smooth-function error is generally of order h². A signed step (b−a)/N follows the interval from a to b. Reversing the limits reverses the integral sign; equal bounds give zero for a finite integrand. These are numerical estimates, not symbolic antiderivatives or certified error bounds.

Reference: github.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Inverse gamma — Cumulative probability
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real InverseGamma.CDF(real shape, real scale, real x)

Returns F(x)=P(X≤x), the accumulated probability through x. A positive distribution obtained by inverting a gamma variable, commonly used for variance modeling.

Definition / convention: f(x)=scale^shape · x^(−shape−1)·exp(−scale/x)/Γ(shape), x>0.

Arguments / value: shape>0 and scale>0. Here scale is the β in exp(−β/x), not a gamma rate argument to be inverted again.

Important: E[X]=scale/(shape−1) exists only for shape>1; finite variance requires shape>2. This is the lower tail. An upper-tail probability is 1−F(x), though that subtraction can lose precision near one.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Inverse gamma — Parameter validity check
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
bool InverseGamma.IsValidParameterSet(real shape, real scale)

Returns a Boolean indicating whether the parameter set passes the library’s validity check; it does not compute a sample or a probability. A positive distribution obtained by inverting a gamma variable, commonly used for variance modeling.

Definition / convention: f(x)=scale^shape · x^(−shape−1)·exp(−scale/x)/Γ(shape), x>0.

Arguments / value: shape>0 and scale>0. Here scale is the β in exp(−β/x), not a gamma rate argument to be inverted again.

Important: E[X]=scale/(shape−1) exists only for shape>1; finite variance requires shape>2. This precheck is not proof of numerical convergence, finite moments, finite precision, or support of every operation. Prefer the finite, nondegenerate model conditions given here, even where the library accepts a limiting case.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Inverse gamma — Probability density f(x)
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real InverseGamma.PDF(real shape, real scale, real x)

Probability density f(x). A positive distribution obtained by inverting a gamma variable, commonly used for variance modeling.

Definition / convention: f(x)=scale^shape · x^(−shape−1)·exp(−scale/x)/Γ(shape), x>0.

Arguments / value: shape>0 and scale>0. Here scale is the β in exp(−β/x), not a gamma rate argument to be inverted again. Evaluate at x; the support is specified above.

Important: E[X]=scale/(shape−1) exists only for shape>1; finite variance requires shape>2. A density is not P(X=x): point probability is zero for a continuous law. Integrate the density over an interval to obtain a probability.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Inverse gamma — Natural logarithm of probability density f(x)

Arguments / value: shape>0 and scale>0. Here scale is the β in exp(−β/x), not a gamma rate argument to be inverted again. Evaluate at x; the support is specified above.

Important: E[X]=scale/(shape−1) exists only for shape>1; finite variance requires shape>2. This is a natural logarithm of the mass/density, not the probability of a logarithmically transformed variable. Zero mass/density has logarithm −∞; direct log evaluation can avoid ordinary underflow.

FunctionInfo.Title: Inverse gamma — One random draw

Syntax

Arguments / value: shape>0 and scale>0. Here scale is the β in exp(−β/x), not a gamma rate argument to be inverted again. rnd is a non-null System.Random instance; its state advances as draws are made.

Important: E[X]=scale/(shape−1) exists only for shape>1; finite variance requires shape>2. Sample values are random, not the density/CDF evaluated at the parameters. Reproducibility requires an explicit generator and a controlled sequence of calls; these are not cryptographic random sources.

FunctionInfo.Title: Inverse Wishart — Parameter validity check
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
bool InverseWishart.IsValidParameterSet(real degreesOfFreedom, Matrix scale)

Returns a Boolean indicating whether the parameter set passes the library’s validity check; it does not compute a sample or a probability. A distribution on symmetric positive-definite matrices, often used as a covariance prior.

Definition / convention: f(X) ∝ |X|^(−(ν+d+1)/2) · exp(−tr(ΨX⁻¹)/2).

Arguments / value: scale=Ψ is a real d×d symmetric positive-definite matrix; degreesOfFreedom=ν>d−1 for a proper nonsingular law.

Important: The scale is Ψ, not the covariance mean. E[X]=Ψ/(ν−d−1) only when ν>d+1. Validation checks do not replace a positive-definite factorization. This precheck is not proof of numerical convergence, finite moments, finite precision, or support of every operation. Prefer the finite, nondegenerate model conditions given here, even where the library accepts a limiting case.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Inverse Wishart — One random draw
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
Matrix InverseWishart.Sample(Random rnd, real degreesOfFreedom, Matrix scale)

Returns one random draw. A distribution on symmetric positive-definite matrices, often used as a covariance prior.

Definition / convention: f(X) ∝ |X|^(−(ν+d+1)/2) · exp(−tr(ΨX⁻¹)/2).

Arguments / value: scale=Ψ is a real d×d symmetric positive-definite matrix; degreesOfFreedom=ν>d−1 for a proper nonsingular law. rnd is a non-null System.Random instance; its state advances as draws are made.

Important: The scale is Ψ, not the covariance mean. E[X]=Ψ/(ν−d−1) only when ν>d+1. Validation checks do not replace a positive-definite factorization. Sample values are random, not the density/CDF evaluated at the parameters. Reproducibility requires an explicit generator and a controlled sequence of calls; these are not cryptographic random sources.

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Jacobi elliptic cn

An elliptic analogue of a trigonometric function, parameterized by m.

Definition / convention: cn(u|m)=cos(am(u|m))

Arguments / value: Real u and −1≤m≤1 in this wrapper. Here m is the PARAMETER k², unlike the modulus argument of EllipticK/E/F.

Important: Identities: sn²+cn²=1 and dn²+m·sn²=1. At m=0, sn=sin, cn=cos and dn=1.
