FunctionInfo.Title: Upper incomplete gamma
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Γ(real a, real x)

The tail of the gamma integral, without division by Γ(a).

Definition / convention: Γ(a,x)=∫ₓ^∞ t^(a−1)exp(−t) dt

Arguments / value: Real a>0 and x≥0; other inputs are rejected by this wrapper.

Important: Alias of gamma with the same convention. Do not confuse this with the lower incomplete gamma or the normalized tails gammaP/gammaQ.

Example: gamma(1,2) ≈ exp(-2)

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Gamma function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real Γ(real x)

The meromorphic extension of the factorial relation to noninteger arguments.

Definition / convention: Γ(z)=∫₀^∞ t^(z−1)e^(−t) dt for Re(z)>0; Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z).

Arguments / value: Simple poles at 0,−1,−2,…; finite negative nonintegers are defined by continuation. Large magnitudes may overflow.

Important: Alias of gamma with the same convention. Γ(n)=(n−1)!, not n!. The complex gamma function is single-valued away from its poles.

Example: gamma(5) = 24

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Gamma function — complex argument
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
complex Γ(complex z)

The meromorphic extension of the factorial relation to noninteger arguments.

Definition / convention: Γ(z)=∫₀^∞ t^(z−1)e^(−t) dt for Re(z)>0; Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z).

Arguments / value: Simple poles at 0,−1,−2,…; finite negative nonintegers are defined by continuation. Large magnitudes may overflow.

Important: Alias of gamma with the same convention. Γ(n)=(n−1)!, not n!. The complex gamma function is single-valued away from its poles.

Example: gamma(5) = 24

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Beta function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real β(real a, real b)

The beta integral; the normalization connecting two gamma factors.

Definition / convention: B(a,b)=∫₀¹ t^(a−1)(1−t)^(b−1)dt = Γ(a)Γ(b)/Γ(a+b)

Arguments / value: Real a>0 and b>0 in this wrapper; symmetric in a and b.

Important: Alias of Beta with the same convention.

Example: Beta(1,1) = 1

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Incomplete beta — legacy parameter-order caveat
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real β(real x, real a, real b)

The intended quantity is the lower beta integral accumulated up to x; the current wrapper passes its arguments in a different order.

Definition / convention: Intended: Bₓ(a,b)=∫₀ˣ t^(a−1)(1−t)^(b−1)dt. Current forwarding: B_b(x,a).

Arguments / value: The visible signature is x,a,b and checks 0≤x≤1, a,b>0, but Meta.Numerics expects a,b,x. The effective integration limit is b, so b>1 can be rejected by the library.

Important: Alias of Beta with the same convention. The wrapper and its β alias call Meta.Numerics.Functions.AdvancedMath.Beta(x,a,b), not Beta(a,b,x). Beta(0.5,1,1) = 2, not the intended 0.5. For Bₓ(a,b), use MathNet.Numerics.SpecialFunctions.BetaIncomplete(a,b,x). This content change does not alter calculations.

Example: MathNet.Numerics.SpecialFunctions.BetaIncomplete(1,1,0.5) = 0.5

Reference: numerics.mathdotnet.com

FunctionInfo.Title: Dirac-delta point helper
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real δ(real x)

A pointwise infinity marker used by this application, not an implementation of a Dirac distribution.

Definition / convention: δ(x)=+∞ when x=0; δ(x)=0 otherwise.

Arguments / value: The mathematical Dirac delta is defined by its action on test functions, not as an ordinary sampled function.

Important: Alias of DiracDelta; it uses the same convention. Do not use this helper to expect unit-area plots or correct quadrature of an impulse. Finite-width approximations or analytic integration are needed.

Example: DiracDelta(0) = Infinity

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Kronecker delta
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real δij(real i, real j)

An equality indicator, distinct from the Dirac delta.

Definition / convention: δij=1 when i=j, and 0 otherwise.

Arguments / value: Inputs are compared using exact floating-point equality, even though the usual notation uses integer indices.

Important: Alias of KroneckerDelta; it uses the same convention.

Example: KroneckerDelta(2,2) = 1

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Hurwitz zeta function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ζ(real x, real q)

Shifts the reciprocal-power series away from the positive integers.

Definition / convention: ζ(s,q)=Σₙ₌₀^∞ (n+q)^(−s)

Arguments / value: The argument named x is the exponent s. This real GSL interface requires s>1 and q>0; it is not the full analytic continuation.

Important: Alias of HurwitzZeta with the same convention.

Example: HurwitzZeta(2,1) ≈ PI*PI/6

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Dirichlet eta function
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real η(real x)

The alternating zeta series, with its removable value supplied at s=1.

Definition / convention: η(s)=Σₙ₌₁^∞ (−1)ⁿ⁻¹/nˢ = (1−2^(1−s))ζ(s)

Arguments / value: Real s; the series converges for s>0, with continuation outside that range.

Important: Alias of DirichletEta with the same convention.

Example: DirichletEta(1) ≈ ln(2)

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Digamma — logarithmic derivative of gamma
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ψ(real x)

The derivative of log Γ, widely used in likelihood equations and harmonic-number identities.

Definition / convention: ψ(z)=Γ′(z)/Γ(z); ψ(n)=Hₙ₋₁−γ for positive integers n.

Arguments / value: Poles at 0,−1,−2,…; use non-pole real or complex arguments.

Important: Alias of psi with the same convention.

Example: psi(1) ≈ -0.5772156649

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Digamma — logarithmic derivative of gamma
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
complex ψ(complex z)

The derivative of log Γ, widely used in likelihood equations and harmonic-number identities.

Definition / convention: ψ(z)=Γ′(z)/Γ(z); ψ(n)=Hₙ₋₁−γ for positive integers n.

Arguments / value: Poles at 0,−1,−2,…; use non-pole real or complex arguments.

Important: Alias of psi with the same convention.

Example: psi(1) ≈ -0.5772156649

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Polygamma of integer order
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ψn(integer n, real x)

The n-th derivative of the digamma function.

Definition / convention: ψ⁽ⁿ⁾(x)=dⁿ⁺¹ lnΓ(x)/dxⁿ⁺¹; ψ⁽⁰⁾=ψ.

Arguments / value: Integer n≥0; avoid gamma poles in x. n=1 is trigamma, n=2 tetragamma.

Important: Alias of polyGamma with the same convention.

Example: polyGamma(1,1) ≈ PI*PI/6

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov

FunctionInfo.Title: Digamma — logarithmic derivative of gamma
FunctionInfo.Description:
Syntax
real ψn(real x)

The derivative of log Γ, widely used in likelihood equations and harmonic-number identities.

Definition / convention: ψ(z)=Γ′(z)/Γ(z); ψ(n)=Hₙ₋₁−γ for positive integers n.

Arguments / value: Poles at 0,−1,−2,…; use non-pole real or complex arguments.

Important: Alias of polyGamma with the same convention. The one-argument polyGamma/ψn/ψⁿ names mean order zero, i.e. digamma, not trigamma.

Example: psi(1) ≈ -0.5772156649

Reference: dlmf.nist.gov
